messages:
charlie_cust: Hey team — after this morning's cert rotation our private endpoint started returning 503s from the SDKs. Errors in app logs: "x509: certificate signed by unknown authority". No infra changes otherwise. Any ideas?

alice_support: Sorry to hear that — can you paste the exact error and which endpoint (VPC/private hostname) you're calling? Did you pin a CA bundle anywhere on the client side?

charlie_cust: Calling `internal-api.acme.example.com:443` (private VPC ALB). SDK log snippet: `rpc: dial tcp: tls: first record does not look like a TLS handshake` then `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority`. We don't manage certs ourselves; we rely on Redwood rotation.

alice_support: Got it. Can you run `openssl s_client -connect internal-api.acme.example.com:443 -showcerts` from a host in the same VPC and paste output? Also confirm whether your app containers have a pinned truststore or custom CA update process.

charlie_cust: Ran the command, here are the cert headers (trimmed):
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
MIIF... (leaf)
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
MIIF... (root)
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
```
No intermediate shown. Our app has an init container that replaces `/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt` with a bundle we generate from a `ConfigMap` at startup. No explicit CA pinning besides that.

bob_sre: That output is the clue — server appears to be sending leaf + root but not the intermediate. Clients that require full chain will fail verification. Do you have any TLS-terminating proxy (nginx / haproxy / envoy) in front of the app that might cache an older cert bundle?

charlie_cust: We use an Nginx ingress in k8s (internal) that proxies to the Redwood private endpoint via a sidecar. We did notice after rotation that the ingress pod restarted.

debbie_eng: FYI rotator-bot shows successful rotation at 2018453500 and pushed the new bundle to the LB. No errors recorded. However, I remember a recent change to the rotator that concatenates intermediate(s) into a single PEM before upload. If separators/newlines are off, some k8s secret mounts or nginx parsing can drop the second cert.

alice_support: Charlie — can you exec into the ingress pod and `cat /etc/ssl/certs/rotated_bundle.pem` (or the mounted secret path) and paste the top 20 lines and bottom 20 lines? That will show whether the intermediate exists in the mounted secret.

charlie_cust: Pulled the file. Top lines: `-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMIIF... (leaf)\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----` Bottom lines immediately after: `-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----MIIF...(intermediate)...-----END CERTIFICATE-----` (note: no newline between `BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----` and the base64)

bob_sre: Ah — missing newline after the `BEGIN CERTIFICATE` header. Many parsers accept it, but some strict parsers (our nginx build) treat that as a single malformed block and drop the intermediate. That explains why `openssl s_client` only saw leaf+root.

debbie_eng: Confirmed. The rotator code path that builds PEM bundles accidentally strips newlines when joining rows for multi-intermediate uploads. We'll patch to preserve `\n` boundaries. I filed ENG-1429 to fix.

alice_support: For a workaround: can you manually update the k8s secret with a corrected PEM (ensure `\n` after `BEGIN CERTIFICATE` and between certs) or mount a variant from a file? Once the ingress has the full chain, clients should verify fine.

charlie_cust: Manual secret update restored connectivity immediately. Apps OK now. Thanks! Can you confirm rotator fix ETA and whether any other customers affected?

debbie_eng: ETA for hotfix deploy: next patch window in ~3 hours; we'll also run a one-off backfill to check recent rotations for malformed joins and contact any affected customers. I'll post updates in #eng-runtime when done.

alice_support: Glad that's resolved. Leaving a follow-up ticket to monitor for any recurrence and we've cc'd your account team to coordinate the backfill. :thumbsup:
